newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KRAJICEK STORMS OUT AS AUSTRALIANS PROSPER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KRAJICEK STORMS OUT AS AUSTRALIANS PROSPER.

text.p: Patrick Rafter and Mark Woodforde ensured the best Australian showing at the French Open since 1969 as Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek angrily joined the lengthy list of men's seeded casualties at Roland Garros on Saturday.

After a string of easy victories for the leading women and American world number two Michael Chang, Rafter and Woodforde both completed magnificent wins to join compatriot Mark Philippoussis among 10 unseeded names in the last 16.
Rafter enjoyed a 6-3 4-6 6-4 6-2 success over Krajicek, a result which left the Dutch sixth seed so disgusted he refused to appear for his post-match press conference and was fined $2,000.

Woodforde, ranked 79 in the world, then guaranteed an all-Australian fourth round meeting with a convincing 6-4 7-6 6-3 victory over 11th seed Albert Costa, merely adding to the sense of gloom among the European clay contingent.

Although moody Chilean Marcelo Rios, seeded seventh, steamed past Arnaud Boetsch in straight sets, the presence of just six seeds in the last 16, one short of the record low set in 1994, suggests the title is as wide open as many predicted beforehand.
Those, however, who felt the men's event would almost certainly be an all-Spanish affair have been proved dramatically wrong.
Neither Woodforde or Philippoussis have ever progressed this far in Paris and there has not been an Australian in the quarter-finals for 15 years.

But after a week of constant sunshine, the red Parisian clay is playing faster than normal and, of the foremost claycourt experts, only Rios and the Spanish duo of Alex Corretja and Sergi Bruguera remain.

"For the other two, it's a natural progression of their stature," said Woodforde, attempting to explain the Australian surge this year. "Both of them are improving very fast, but I don't know what my excuse is to be in the fourth round."

Defending champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov is still lurking in the top half of the draw but the most significant fourth round encounter in the bottom half looks set to be the showdown between former champions Chang and Bruguera.
Chang disposed of his third successive French opponent when Stephane Simian retired with a groin strain at 5-2 in the second set, and looks in an increasingly determined mood.
"Whenever you play Sergi on clay you know it's going to be tough. He's had a lot of success here but I'm looking forward to it," said Chang. "There are definitely going to be a lot of long points."
South African 13th seed Wayne Ferreira did not even make it on court for his third round match against Petr Korda of the Czech Republic.
Ferreira twisted an ankle in practice on Friday, allowing Korda to book his first French Open fourth round berth since reaching the final in 1992.
The top women were all involved in a succession of mis-matches as they progressed to the last 16 without dropping a set or, in some cases, breaking into a sweat.
Hingis, the women's world number one, was arguably the most impressive, flattening her teenage rival Anna Kournikova 6-1 6-3 to maintain her unbeaten record this year.
Kournikova was powerless against the variety of Hingis's strokes, holding out for only 42 minutes in what had been billed as a showdown between two potential champions of the next millennium.
Hingis will be back in action on Sunday against 16th seed Barbara Paulus of Austria while Monica Seles is due to face Mary Pierce, the sole French survivor.

Seles, the triple French champion between 1990 and 1992, required 51 minutes to steamroller Nathalie Tauziat 6-0 6-1, being detained only briefly at the end of the first set when the French player saved six set points.
The contest was so one-sided that when Tauziat finally won a game midway through the second set she raised her arms aloft in mock triumph, but by then Seles was already looking ahead.
"I can't play defensively against Mary because she hits the ball really hard," said Seles. "She'll just blow me off the court."
Sixth seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario was another rapid winner, 6-0 6-3 over Dominique Van Roost of Belgium, and now meets Natasha Zvereva who downed 14th seed Brenda Schultz-McCarthy 7-6 6-4.
